text:
What do you seek from us, O sea, with your
+teaching volumes! How inconsolable, how atrocious
+you are in the feverish suntrap.
+
+With your hoes you leap,
+with your leaves you leap,
+axing, axing in mad sesame,
+while the waves return weeping, after
+unshoeing the four winds
+and all memories, in lipped platters
+of tungsten, contractions of fangs
+and static chelonian els.
+
+Philosophy of black wings vibrating
+at the fearful trembling of the day’s shoulders.
+
+The sea, and an edition standing,
+upon its single sheet the recto
+facing the verso.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem LXIX — What Do You Seek from Us, O Sea
translation.editorial_note: Volumes and hojas retain the sea’s simultaneous book and material mass; descalcar becomes unshoeing, while the typographic els remain turtle-like chelonians.
